summary.short: EU semiconductor ecosystem framework: creates the Chips for Europe Initiative and a European Semiconductor Board, lets the Commission recognise first-of-a-kind integrated production facilities and open EU foundries, and sets monitoring and crisis-stage powers, including priority-rated orders. Enters into force on the third day after OJ publication; directly applicable.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2023/1781 sets a framework for the EU semiconductor ecosystem. It establishes the Chips for Europe Initiative, funded from Horizon Europe and the Digital Europe Programme and implemented mainly by the Chips Joint Undertaking, with five operational objectives (design platform, pilot lines, quantum chips, competence centres, Chips Fund). It lets the Commission recognise first-of-a-kind integrated production facilities and open EU foundries, which may receive Member State support and then accept priority-rated orders in a crisis. Chapter IV requires strategic mapping, monitoring and early warning indicators, and allows a Council-activated crisis stage of up to 12 months with information requests, priority-rated orders and common purchasing. It creates a European Semiconductor Board and national competent authorities. Fines reach EUR 300 000 for incorrect information, EUR 150 000 for unreported third-country obligations (EUR 50 000 for SMEs), and periodic penalty payments reach 1,5 % of daily turnover for priority-rated orders (0,5 % for SMEs).

‘semiconductor’ means one of the following:
‘chip’ means an electronic device comprising various functional elements on a single piece of semiconductor material
‘quantum chip’ means a device that processes information at the level of individual quantum systems
‘semiconductor supply chain’ means the system of activities, organisations, actors, technology, information, resources and services involved in the production of semiconductors
‘semiconductor value chain’ means the set of activities in relation to a semiconductor product from its conception to its end use
‘pilot line’ means an experimental project or action addressing higher technology readiness levels from levels 3 to 8

definitions.defined_in: Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC, Article 2 of the Annex (by reference, in this Regulation Art. 2(9))

evidence.quote: ‘small and medium-sized enterprises’ or ‘SMEs’ means small or medium-sized enterprises as defined in Article 2 of the Annex to Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC

definitions.defined_in: Regulation (EU) 2021/695, Article 2, point (20) (by reference, in this Regulation Art. 2(10))

evidence.quote: ‘small mid-cap’ means small mid-cap as defined in Article 2, point (20), of Regulation (EU) 2021/695
‘first-of-a-kind facility’ means a new or substantially upgraded semiconductor manufacturing facility
‘next-generation semiconductor technologies’ means semiconductor technologies that go beyond the state of the art
‘cutting-edge semiconductor technologies’ means state-of-the-art innovation in chips and semiconductor technologies when the projects are carried out
‘semiconductor manufacturing’ means any of the stages of production and processing of semiconductor wafers
‘production capability’ means the ability of a facility to produce certain types of products
‘production capacity’ means the maximum potential output of a facility
‘users of semiconductors’ means undertakings that produce products in which semiconductors are incorporated
‘key market actors’ means undertakings in the Union’s semiconductor supply chain, the reliable functioning of which is essential for the supply of semiconductors
‘critical sector’ means any sector referred to in Annex IV
‘crisis-relevant product’ means semiconductors, intermediate products and raw and processed materials
A semiconductor crisis shall be considered to occur where:
a legal entity may be established in the form of a European chips infrastructure consortium (ECIC)
The Commission may award a label of ‘design centre of excellence’ to design centres established in the Union
an order of crisis-relevant products (priority-rated order)
for their public procurement of crisis-relevant products for critical sectors (common purchasing)

obligations.summary: The Commission must provide standardised and secure means for collecting, processing and storing information acquired under the Regulation.

evidence.quote: The Commission shall provide for standardised and secure means for the collection, processing and storage of the information acquired

obligations.summary: The Commission must hear the undertaking concerned, on preliminary findings and intended measures, before adopting a penalty decision.
obligations.conditional_on: Before adopting a penalty decision under Art. 33

evidence.quote: Before adopting a decision pursuant to Article 33, the Commission shall give the undertaking concerned the opportunity of being heard

obligations.summary: The European Semiconductor Board must hold ordinary meetings at least once a year.

evidence.quote: The European Semiconductor Board shall hold ordinary meetings at least once a year.

obligations.summary: The Commission must inform the European Semiconductor Board regularly on progress in implementing operational objective 5 (Chips Fund activities).

evidence.quote: The Commission shall inform the European Semiconductor Board on progress in the implementation of the Initiative’s operational objective 5

obligations.summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts to amend Annex I (actions) and Annex II (measurable indicators) under Art. 37.

evidence.quote: the Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 37 to amend Annex I

obligations.summary: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission must consult experts designated by each Member State, under the Interinstitutional Agreement of 13 April 2016.
obligations.conditional_on: Adoption of a delegated act

evidence.quote: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State

obligations.summary: By 20 September 2026 and every four years thereafter, the Commission must submit a report on evaluation and review of the Regulation to the European Parliament and the Council, to be made public.

evidence.quote: the Commission shall submit a report on the evaluation and review of this Regulation to the European Parliament and to the Council

obligations.summary: For evaluation and review, the European Semiconductor Board, Member States and national competent authorities must provide the Commission with information on its request.
obligations.conditional_on: Commission request for information for evaluation and review

evidence.quote: the European Semiconductor Board, the Member States and national competent authorities shall provide the Commission with information on its request.

enforcement.triggered_by: Undertaking, intentionally or through gross negligence, supplies incorrect, incomplete or misleading information in response to a Commission information request under Art. 25, or does not supply the information within the prescribed time limit
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Fines shall not exceed EUR 300 000; where the undertaking is an SME, the fines shall not exceed EUR 50 000
enforcement.penalty_formula: Fixed ceiling of EUR 300 000. The SME ceiling of EUR 50 000 is stated in the same paragraph (Art. 33(3)). Amount set by Commission decision considering nature, gravity and duration (Art. 33(5)).
enforcement.cure_period: None stated. Art. 33(2) requires the Commission to hear the undertaking before a decision, and Art. 33(5) requires account to be taken of partial compliance where applicable.

evidence.quote: Fines imposed in the cases referred to in paragraph 1, point (a), shall not exceed EUR 300 000.

enforcement.triggered_by: Undertaking, intentionally or through gross negligence, does not comply with the obligation to inform the Commission of a third-country obligation pursuant to Art. 25(7) and Art. 26(3)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Fines shall not exceed EUR 150 000; where the undertaking is an SME, the fines shall not exceed EUR 50 000
enforcement.penalty_formula: Fixed ceiling of EUR 150 000. The SME ceiling of EUR 50 000 is stated in the same paragraph (Art. 33(3)).
enforcement.cure_period: None stated. Art. 33(2) requires the Commission to hear the undertaking before a decision.

evidence.quote: Fines imposed in the cases referred to in paragraph 1, point (b), shall not exceed EUR 150 000.

enforcement.triggered_by: Undertaking, intentionally or through gross negligence, does not comply with an obligation to prioritise the production of crisis-relevant products under Art. 26 (periodic penalty payments)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Periodic penalty payments shall not exceed 1,5 % of the current daily turnover for each working day of non-compliance; for an SME, 0,5 % of the current daily turnover
enforcement.penalty_formula: 1,5 % of current daily turnover per working day of non-compliance, counted from the date established in the decision issuing the priority-rated order; SME ceiling 0,5 % of current daily turnover. Commission may fix a lower definitive amount once the requirements are fulfilled (Art. 33(6)).
enforcement.cure_period: None stated. Art. 33(6) allows the definitive amount to be set lower where the undertaking has fulfilled the requirements the penalty was intended to enforce.

evidence.quote: Periodic penalty payments imposed in the case referred to in paragraph 1, point (c), shall not exceed 1,5 % of the current daily turnover for each working day of non-compliance
